name.text: Numbering the faces of a die to give probabilities

questiontext.text:
A blank die has six faces. Write a whole number from 1 to 9 on each face (numbers may repeat) so that, when the die is rolled,

\(P(\text{even number}) = \dfrac{{@nev@}}{6}\) and \(P(\text{number greater than } {@m@}) = \dfrac{{@k@}}{6}\).

Each fraction is out of 6 because the die has six faces.

Give your six numbers as a list, for example [1,2,2,5,8,9].

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Decide how many faces of each kind you need, then choose numbers. You need \({@nev@}\) even faces and \({@k@}\) faces greater than \({@m@}\). A number such as 8 is both even and greater than \({@m@}\), so it counts for both.

One way: \({@a@}\) faces showing 8 (even and greater than \({@m@}\)), \({@nev-a@}\) showing 2 (even, not greater), \({@k-a@}\) showing 9 (odd, greater) and \({@6-nev-k+a@}\) showing 1 (odd, not greater). That gives the die \({@ta@}\).

Any list of six numbers from 1 to 9 with the right counts is accepted. Remember that greater than \({@m@}\) does not include \({@m@}\) itself.

falsefeedback.text: Your die has \({@ne@}\) even faces, so \(P(\text{even})\) would be \(\dfrac{{@ne@}}{6}\). You need \({@nev@}\) even faces.

truefeedback.text: You counted faces showing \({@m@}\). Greater than \({@m@}\) does not include \({@m@}\).

falsefeedback.text: Your die has \({@ng@}\) faces greater than \({@m@}\), so that probability would be \(\dfrac{{@ng@}}{6}\). You need \({@k@}\).
